items.text: Every licensed agent has an NPN you can look up on NIPR's producer database before you ever talk to them. Ours is 21370662. We'd rather you verify us than take our word for it.

Anyone can say "licensed and independent" in a bio. Here is how to actually check.

Every insurance producer has a National Producer Number, issued and tracked through NIPR, the industry's own licensing database. You can look up any agent's NPN and see exactly which states they are licensed in and whether that license is active, before you ever get on a call with them.

Ours is 21370662, licensed across 11 states. We put it on our materials on purpose, because it is checkable, and because most of the people we talk to have never been offered a way to verify anyone before.

The other thing worth checking: is the agent tied to a single carrier's call center, or independent? An independent agent can show you options across companies and tell you when the plan you already have is the right one to keep. A captive agent, by definition, cannot.

Verification and independence are the two things we think a serious agency should make easy to check, not just claim.

Honorbrook Insurance, Tysons VA. honorbrook-insurance.com
